extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, analysts, and philosophers concerned with the foundations and rigor of calculus (readers of 18th-century mathematical criticism / instructors of mathematical rigor)
extracted.subtask_description: A normative critique of the principles and methods of the modern analysis (fluxions/infinitesimals), listing standards for clear, legitimate mathematical reasoning and acceptable use of notation, limits, and diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of definitions, postulates, and axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Definitions are clear; when the Postulata cannot be refused, nor the Axioms denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Berkeley emphasizes that geometry is 'an excellent Logic' only when definitions, postulata, and axioms are clear and indisputable; clear objects and fixed attention yield exact, methodical reasoning transferable to other inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly conceived object of geometry (assignable extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Object of Geometry be not the Proportions of aſsignable Extenſions? And whether there be any need of considering Quantities either infinitely great or infinitely ſmall?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries urge that geometry's aim should be finite, assignable magnitudes and proportions; introducing infinite or infinitesimal objects is questioned as unnecessary and source of difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine mathematical principles with free, critical inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Their Principles and Methods to be examined with the ſame Freedom, which they aſſume with regard to the Principles and Myſteries of Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author claims mathematicians' methods must be open to scrutiny rather than accepted on deference or authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy and clarity of fluxions (definition and conception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluxions ... What theſe Fluxions are; Fluxions placed in various Lights ... fluxions sometimes in one sense, sometimes another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluxions must be clearly and consistently defined (e.g. as velocities, increments, or moments); shifting or multiple conceptions of fluxions is unacceptable because it produces emptiness and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moments/infinitesimals must have clear ontological status
rubrics_metrics.description: By Moments we are not to understand finite Particles. Theſe are ſaid not to be Moments, but Quantities generated from Moments ... the Moments are only the naſcent Principles of finite Quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moments (nascent increments) are distinguished from finite particles; their nature is hard to conceive and must be explicitly clarified if admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not retain consequences derived from a supposition after contradicting that supposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If with a View to demonſtrate ... a certain Point is ſuppoſed, by virtue of which certain other Points are attained; and such ſuppoſed Point be itſelf afterwards deſtroyed ... the other Points ... muſt alſo be deſtroyed and rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is invalid to assume increments exist to compute ratios and then 'let the increments vanish' while keeping algebraic consequences obtained under the former assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform meaning of symbols (no shifting of signification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs may be made to denote either any thing or Nothing: And conſequently that in the original Notation x, o might have ſignified either an Increment or nothing. But then which of theſe ſoever you make it ſignify, you muſt argue conſiſtently with ſuch its Signification, and not proceed upon a double meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation must have a single consistent interpretation within a demonstration; allowing symbols to mean something in one step and nothing in the next is sophistical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of right reason apply equally in symbols and in words
rubrics_metrics.description: The ſame Rules of right Reaſon to be obſerved, whether Men argue in Symbols or in Words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic (algebraic/fluxional) manipulations are subject to the same logical standards as verbal deductive proofs; algebraic convenience does not excuse logical lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deriving principles from their conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The inverted Way of demonſtrating your Principles by your Concluſions ... The Truth of the Concluſion will not prove either the Form or the Matter of a Syllogiſm to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One cannot justify foundational principles by appealing to the correctness of their consequences; principles must be established independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent suppositions (cannot reason from contradictory premises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is plainer than that no juſt Concluſion can be directly drawn from two inconſiſtent Suppoſitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical reasoning must not mix incompatible assumptions (for example, that an increment both exists and does not exist) within a single line of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject higher-order terms without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is plain that the direct and true Method ... yields the true increment ... exceeding that which was obtained by the former illegitimate and indirect Method by the Quantity ab. And it is not enough to say ab is exceedingly small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dropping products of small increments (higher-order infinitesimals) must be logically justified; one cannot dismiss ab purely because it is 'exceeding small' unless the principles permit neglect of such errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits are not quantities; be careful in attributing magnitude to limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Points or mere Limits of naſcent Lines are undoubtedly equal, as having no more Magnitude one than another, a Limit as ſuch being no Quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A limit should be treated as a boundary notion, not as a finite magnitude; conflating limits with quantities causes confusion in fluxional reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid infinite regress of infinitesimals without foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: They conſider Quantities infinitely leſs than the leaſt diſcernible Quantity; and others infinitely leſs than thoſe infinitely ſmall ones ... an infinite Succeſſion of Infiniteſimals ... which you till approach and never arrive at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postulating an endless hierarchy of infinitesimals (first, second, third, ... ad infinitum) demands justification; using such an ontology implicitly without foundation is suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notational clarity: distinguish exponents/signs from fluxions
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs or Exponents obvious; but Fluxions themselves not so ... Fluxions, whether the Velocities with which infiniteſimal Differences are generated, or ... Fluxions of Fluxions ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation like x, dx, ddx, exponents and fluxional marks must not be conflated; ambiguity between exponentiation and fluxional notation leads to error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagrams are signs of all possible finite figures (do not treat them as actual infinite objects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Diagrams in a Geometrical Demonſtration are not to be conſidered, as Signs of all poſſible finite Figures, of all ſenible and imaginable Extenſions or Magnitudes of the ſame Kind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometrical diagrams represent generic finite instances and should not be read as literal carriers of infinite parts or infinitesimals in themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not suppose finite extension is infinitely divisible as a necessary truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be neceſſary, as well as abſurd, to ſuppose that finite Extenſion is infinitely diviſible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question the assumption of infinite divisibility of lengths/areas; treating finite extension as inherently containing infinitely many parts is philosophically and methodologically problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportions involving nothing are nonsensical
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Nothings can be conſidered as proportional to real Quantities? Or whether to talk of their Proportions be not to talk Nonſenſe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about 'proportions of increments when increments vanish' must avoid treating 'nothing' as an object of proportion; proportions presuppose quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic rules must be interpreted cautiously in geometric contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether becauſe, in the general Caſe of pure Algebra, we are at full liberty to  ... denote either a positive or a negative Quantity, or nothing at all, therefore in a Geometrical Caſe, limited Hypotheſes and Reaſonings ... claim the ſame Licence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic liberties with signs and symbols do not automatically carry over to geometrical reasoning about specific finite magnitudes; domain/context matters for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shifting the hypothesis (supposition shifting) is a sophism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Shifting of the Hypotheſes (or as we may call it the fallacia suppoſirionis) be not a Sophifm, that far and wide infeſts the modern Reafonings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the assumed meaning of a hypothesis mid-argument (e.g. treating an increment first as nonzero, then as zero) is illicit and undermines the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental rules (like product rule for fluxions) must be derived legitimately
rubrics_metrics.description: The main Point in the Method of Fluxions is to obtain the Fluxion or Momentum of the Rectangle or Product of two indeterminate Quantities ... this fundamental Point ... one would think should be very clearly made out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core derivations (product rule, power rule) should be given transparent, logically sound demonstrations rather than heuristic or inconsistent manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept useful rules as proofs of their foundational soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Man by Methods, not geometrical or demonstrative, shall have satisfied himself of the Usefulness of certain Rules ... such his Disciples may ... confound the Usefulness of a Rule with the Certainty of a Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical success or computational efficacy of rules does not substitute for rigorous justification of principles; usefulness isn't proof of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between nascent/evanescent increments and infinitesimals
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard to distinguish between evaneſcent Increments and infiniteſimal Differences. Fluxions placed in various Lights. The great Author ... not ſatisfied with his own Notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts must clarify whether they mean nascent/instantaneous increments (moments), finite but small increments, or true infinitesimals; conflation creates paradox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about whether approximations or exact demonstrations are intended
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be righter to approximate fairly, than to endeavour at Ac­curacy by falſe Prin­ciples? Whether it not be more decent to try Trials and Inductions, than to pretend to demonſtrate by falſe Principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one uses heuristics/approximations, state that goal; do not masquerade approximate or inductive methods as exact demonstrations from invalid principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating velocity or motion as a property of a mere limit point
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Motion can be perceived in a Point of Space? And if Motion cannot, whether Velocity can? And if not, whether a first or last Velocity can be conceived in a mere Limit; either Initial or Final?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conception of instantaneous velocity or motion at a bare limit requires careful metaphysical/epistemic grounding; do not attribute properties to pure limits without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and symbolic devices must not mask emptiness or contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If we remove the Veil and look under­neath, if laying aſide the Expreſſions we ſet ourſelves attentively to consider the things themſelves, which are ſuppoſed to be expreſſed or marked thereby, we ſhall diſcover much Emptineſs, Darkneſs, and Confuſion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notational convenience should not hide that the purported objects (infinitesimals, nascent increments) lack clear content; insist on interpreting symbols in terms of intelligible entities or limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematicians should be modest outside their proper sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: …the Employment of modern Analysts, however useful in Mathematical Calculations, … doth not habituate and qualify the Mind to apprehend clearly and infer justly; and consequently, that you have no Right in Virtue of such Habits, to dictate out of your proper Sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical skill in computation does not automatically confer epistemic authority in unrelated domains; caution and modesty are recommended when crossing fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concluding that true conclusions vindicate faulty intermediate reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: That Men may arrive at Truth by virtue of error ... Error may bring forth Truth, though it cannot bring forth Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correct theorem reached via fallacious premises does not justify the premises; true results obtained by bad logic do not make the method scientific.
